messages:
anya: Heads up — proposing a change to routing config for a few routes: add a per-route 'preference_ttl' (how long to keep preferring a region after a success), plus a 'route_tag' that we hoist into headers so quotas/observability can attribute requests. Sketch below. Thoughts?

anya: ```yaml
route: /v1/generate
match: POST
regionalPreference: [local, us-west-2, us-east-1]
preference_ttl: 30s  # keep preferring local for 30s after a success
hoist_headers: [x-rw-route-tag, x-rw-region-priority]
route_tag: tenant-api-v2
fallback_policy: latency_then_cost
```

raf: quick q — if client sends `x-rw-preferred-region`, does that override the TTL-based preference? precedence?

anya: good call. I think header overrides should have top precedence but only if the header is signed/trusted (internal key). otherwise we ignore. TTL only affects internal decision cache.

sam: agree on signed headers. also please add telemetry fields: routing.decision, routing.reason, routing.ttl_remaining, routing.route_tag. we need those in traces + metrics for alerting.

kira: UI/UX ask: in Console can we show the effective fallback chain + current TTL state for a route? oncall needs to see why traffic moved to fallback region during incidents. maybe a tiny timeline on the route page.

marco: watch out for quotas. If we hoist route_tag into headers and use that for per-route quotas, a noisy route_tag value change could create billing/fair-usage churn. We should enforce an allowlist and max length.

anya: noted. enforce allowlist + stable IDs only. make the Console only allow creating route_tags from a controlled dropdown (no freeform).

ops-bot: :information_source: routing-config-validator: detected no allowlist for route_tag on route /v1/generate in staging. Marked WARNING.

raf: another edge: what about caching at edge? If region preference is hoisted as header, we might break shared CDN caching. Maybe set `Cache-Vary` to include hoisted header only for internal caches.

sam: yes, we must avoid exposing hoisted headers to client caches. set `Surrogate-Control` and `Vary` appropriately and strip before responding externally.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: feature/route-ttl-hoist -> staging (canary 10%). manual approval required for console changes.

kira: for the Console timeline: small checkbox to enable 'show routing timeline' per route + export button. also need an 'override' button that oncall can use to temporarily bump preference_ttl to >0 for an hour. audit log entry required.

marco: also add a quota-mapping doc: route_tag -> billing_key -> quota_bucket. keep mapping immutable once created so we don't break historical billing.

anya: action items: 1) implement header hoist but only for allowlisted route_tags and signed headers, 2) emit routing.* telemetry to tracing + metrics, 3) Console: routing timeline + temporary TTL override with audit log, 4) CDN rules: do not expose hoisted headers to external caches. I'll open PRs for runtime + telemetry. assigning followups in the ticket. :thumbsup:

raf: LGTM. small nit: preference_ttl should be configurable per-customer and per-route. some customers want 5m.

anya: agreed — default 30s, max configurable per plan. I'll include that in the design doc.

sam: I'll add the tracing fields and a dashboard draft for routing anomalies (sudden increase in fallback_rate).

anya: thanks team — will document and loop in security for header signing details.
